17 Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. (Matthew 5:17 KJV)

Jesus needed to tell people His purpose for coming, and since He was preaching mercy and grace, He needed to let people know that He was fulfilling the Law. By His fulfilling the whole law, and living a completely sinless life (1 Peter 2:22), He was able to become the perfect sacrifice that did fulfill the requirements of the law for all our sins (1 John 2:2). Jesus didn’t do away with the law, but just lived it. Once the Law was fulfilled, and the perfect sacrifice was made, then the Law no longer had control of our lives. Since the Law was what made sin come alive (Romans 7:9), the fulfilling of the Law did away with sin. Christians should not be sin conscious at all now (Hebrews 10:2).

The Law is still in effect for all those who do not accept Jesus as their Savior, as they are turning down His sacrifice for their sins. Sins have been totally done away with as far as God is concerned, and that means for the whole world (1 John 2:2). The only sin that will send a non-believer to hell is the sin of rejecting Jesus, and anyone who does so, deserves what they will get. To scorn the tremendous sacrifice of Jesus is by far the worse sin anyone could ever commit. Make Jesus your Savior (Romans 10:9-10), and don’t blasphemy the Holy Ghost (Matthew 12:31-32) or become reprobate (Romans 1:28), or disobey Jesus (Hebrews 5:9), and you will make it to heaven – Praise God.
